A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison. The approximate-unlearning study moves from v1 Appendix C to v2 Section 5.6; the original examples and limitations are retained.

before.justification: v1 reports original extraction experiments on MUSE, TOFU, WMDP and synthetic medical records, including benchmark results, ablations, defenses and approximate-unlearning evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds LoRA, Mixtral and ETHICIST experiments in Appendices C–E and Tables 4–6.

M1.justification: The reversed-guidance and token-filter procedure in Equations 2–5 is unchanged. Appendix E adds an evaluated variant combining the attack with ETHICIST, a limited procedural extension reported as 'Ours + ETHICIST' in Table 6.

E1.justification: The datasets and extraction tasks remain MUSE, TOFU, WMDP and synthetic medical records. Appendix E adds a stronger side-information scenario in which the attacker accesses half the TOFU retain set to train soft prompts. The LoRA and Mixtral additions otherwise concern model configurations rather than new data coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds ETHICIST as an evaluated extraction comparator in Appendix E/Table 6. The existing pre- and post-unlearning generation comparisons and approximate-unlearning comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Appendices C–E substantially extend the evaluated configurations: Phi-1.5 with LoRA for five epochs at learning rate 2e-4 and guidance 1.6; Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 with LoRA for two epochs, cosine scheduling from 1e-4 and guidance 2; and soft-prompt training using half the retain set for ETHICIST. These are added protocols, not revisions to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Table 6 adds a component-combination analysis comparing ETHICIST, the proposed attack and their combination to test complementarity. The original guidance/filter sweeps, forgetting-ratio and epoch analyses, defenses, approximate-unlearning analysis and illustrative cases remain; moving the approximate-unlearning study does not add new evidence.

E5.justification: Both Table 1 captions report three unlearning runs, A-ESR standard deviation below 0.01 and omission of deviations from the table. The new checklist repeats this disclosure. No new run counts, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests are reported for the added experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the original figures retain their results, while Tables 4–6 substantially extend the evidence. Newly reported A-ESR1.0 is 0.108 versus pre-unlearning generation's 0.055 for Phi-LoRA, and 0.055 versus 0.018 for Mixtral-LoRA. Table 6 reports 0.073 for ETHICIST, 0.120 for the proposed attack and 0.153 for their combination. These are additional comparisons under their stated settings.

T1.justification: The metric definition and guidance/filter mathematics in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. No new theorem, proof or derivation appears. The added checklist characterizes Section 4 as heuristic modeling without changing its mathematics.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that access to pre- and post-unlearning models enables guidance and filtering to increase extraction, sometimes doubling success. The revised title and abstract emphasize exposure more explicitly, but this condition was already stated in v1. The contribution list and conclusion retain the same substantive claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly explains ETHICIST's complementarity with guidance: single-model extraction can combine with information from differences between model states. It also qualifies the comparison by identifying ETHICIST's additional training-data access. The original mechanism explanations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code statement and repository pointer in the abstract, identifies the Mixtral checkpoint, and documents training schedules and guidance settings for the added experiments. It specifies the retained-data allocation for ETHICIST and refers to its original code for hyperparameters. Existing hardware and dataset-preparation disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to LoRA, Mixtral of Experts and ETHICIST, together with a focused discussion positioning ETHICIST as complementary to the proposed attack. The main related-work discussion otherwise remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are revised, author affiliation and publication-header information change, and acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist are added. The approximate-unlearning section moves into the main text, and new appendices precede the retained visualization and limitations sections. Most existing prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–6 and moves Table 3 from the appendix into the main text. Existing plots and surrounding text are redistributed across pages, while the original figures, table designs and example visualizations are retained. There is no wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The LoRA and Mixtral experiments broaden empirical support, while the ETHICIST comparison and combination strengthen evaluation beyond direct generation baselines. The code-access pointer and clearer exposure-focused abstract also help. These are incremental gains: the additional experiments remain confined to TOFU, ETHICIST uses extra retained-data access, and the original uncertainty reporting and applicability limitations remain.
